newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares down on NATO news, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares down on NATO news, seen falling.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell for the seventh straight session on Friday, plummeting 2.85 percent after news that the U.S. appeared unlikely to back Slovenia's bid for early NATO membership.
"Our market is so depressed and illiquid that each piece of good or bad news has a big impact on prices," said one broker.

Analysts said the market had hoped for Slovenia to be included in NATO as soon as possible since that would increase the country's credibility abroad and help lure more foreign investors to the small market.
The SBI index fell 2.85 percent or 36.23 points to close at 1,235.63, taking this week's overall loss to 5.62 percent.
Overall 14 shares fell, two rose and three were flat, while nine were untraded. Turnover eased to 57.9 million tolars from 76.4 million.

Market participants said prices were likely to continue easing gradually over the summer, but added that further declines could make for some profitable buying opportunities and lift the index in the short term.

"I already started thinking about buying as prices are so low and I don't think I am the only one thinking that way -- so maybe prices may rise a bit next week," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza.
Drug maker Lek had the day's highest turnover, tumbling 8.97 percent to 22,030 tolars on volume of 867 shares for total turnover of 19.5 million tolars.
Traders attributed the fall to the share going ex-dividend and said the stock was likely to bottom out at 22,000 tolars.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 9.37 percent to 7,160 tolars on volume of 29 shares. Traders attributed the fall to a technical reaction to an 11.3 percent gain since Wednesday.

Trading volumes in Dadas have been poor since March last year, when the Securities Market Agency started procedures to ban Dadas' brokerage arm from trading, claiming it was rigging prices among its affiliated companies.
Since then the share has fallen over 95 percent, while average daily volume dropped to about 50 shares a day from over 1,000 shares per day previously.
Bank Hipotekarna Banka Brezice was the top gainer, rising 3.80 percent to 4,100 tolars on volume of only one share.
